para.text: In a 2D world a position is presented by 2 parameters. These parameters depend on the co-ordinate system, and in most cases a linear rectangular co-ordinate system is chosen (Cartesian co-ordinates). In a plane these co-ordinates are represented by two axes, generally called X and Y axis as shown in the figure.

para.text: In a 3D world a third parameter is required to obtain a certain position. For this the flat 2D Cartesian co-ordinate system is extended by a third axis, generally called Z, and by convention the positive Z-direction points upwards from the standard X-Y plane, see figure. Note that there exist other co-ordinate systems as well like cylindrical or spherical co-ordinates, see

para.text: A 3D world cannot be drawn on a flat plane. It can only be projected on a flat plane, and the result depends on the characteristics of the projection. In many cases a certain viewing position is selected, and the projection of the world on the plane is such that a position on that plane corresponds with a certain viewing direction, and ‘up’ in the world is also ‘up’ in the plane of projection.
